title: Africa · breeds of the continent
blurb: From the Atlas to the Cape: the Basenji, the ridgeback and the landraces that never needed a kennel club to survive.

items.d: Central African hunter that barks almost never, cleans itself like a cat and carries a curled tail.
Southern African hound with a ridge of reversed hair, bred to trail lions and guard the homestead.
South Africa's farm guard: 70–90 kg of mastiff, bred to hold a gate and a family.
The free-living dog of southern Africa, a landrace rather than a breed, shaped by the veld.
West African sighthound of the Sahel: tall, thin-skinned and built to run down gazelle in heat.
North Africa's smooth sighthound, kept by the Berbers for hare and gazelle.
Moroccan Atlas guard dog with a heavy coat, kept with flocks against wolves.
Madagascar's cotton-coated companion from the port of Toliara, 4–6 kg.
